articles.title: Warning Issued Over Trespassing at Abandoned Asbestos Factory in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Landowners of the derelict Turner Brothers factory have warned trespassers of the dangers posed by the site, which has been a hotspot for urban explorers.
articles.content_html:
Landowners of the abandoned Turner Brothers factory in Rochdale have issued a warning to trespassers regarding the dangers of entering the site. The factory, located in the Spotland area, has been derelict for decades and is known for hazardous conditions, including the presence of asbestos.

Spodden Park Ltd, the company responsible for the site, anticipates an increase in trespassing activity during the summer holidays. They expressed concern about potential fires being started on the premises, particularly given the dry weather conditions in the region. The company has stated that breaking into the site is a criminal offence and that they will contact the police if their security measures detect any intrusions.

The site has become a popular location for 'urban explorers', many of whom may not be aware of the risks involved. Experts warn that asbestos fibres still present in the buildings can lead to serious health issues, including asbestosis and lung cancer. Spodden Park Ltd has urged parents to educate their children about the dangers of trespassing and the potential consequences of being caught.

In addition to the health risks, the deteriorating state of the buildings poses a risk of collapse, making it difficult for emergency services to respond to any incidents. The company has repaired the perimeter security fence and continues to take measures to secure the site, while also planning for future redevelopment.

articles.title: Joe Hickey Joins North Wales Crusaders on Loan
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Hornets half-back Joe Hickey has been loaned to North Wales Crusaders until the end of the season to gain more playing experience.
articles.content_html:
A half-back has joined North Wales Crusaders on loan until the end of the season. Joe Hickey, who joined Rochdale Hornets in October last year, will be looking to gain further game time during his spell with the Crusaders.

Hickey impressed at reserve grade level for Warrington Wolves during the 2025 campaign and has made six appearances for the Hornets this season. His appearances include two in the Betfred Challenge Cup, one in the 1895 Cup, and three in the Championship.

The club has sanctioned the move to support Hickey's development, while retaining the option to recall him if necessary. His last appearance for the Hornets was in May against Goole Vikings.

Everyone at the club wishes Joe well with the move as he seeks to enhance his experience on the field.

articles.title: Rochdale and Northampton Town Draw 0-0 in League Two Clash
articles.excerpt: Rochdale played to a 0-0 draw against Northampton Town in their EFL League Two match on Saturday. The match, held at Spotland, saw both teams struggle to find the back of the net despite several attempts.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale played to a 0-0 draw against Northampton Town in their EFL League Two match on Saturday.

The match, held at Spotland, saw both teams struggle to find the back of the net despite several attempts.

Rochdale will look to improve their performance in upcoming fixtures as they aim to climb the league table.

The result leaves Rochdale with a point as they continue their campaign in the 2026/27 season.
